dedupe_keys.name: un ggce hidden risk report on the global geodesy supply chain 2024

description: Hidden Risk is a background report for decision makers, published in June 2024 by the United Nations Global Geodetic Centre of Excellence, on how weaknesses in the global geodesy supply chain could have severe effects on critical infrastructure and national economies. Geodesy provides the reference frames, precise satellite orbits and clocks and Earth orientation parameters that satellite positioning, navigation and timing depend on; these come from a global network of ground observatories, analysis centres and data centres run largely by research institutions on short-term funding. The report explains how infrastructure such as power grids, telecommunications, finance, transport, agriculture and emergency services depends on GNSS and therefore on geodesy, summarises estimates of the economic benefits and of the costs of losing satellite services, describing a day without satellites, and sets out five major weaknesses: too little evidence of its importance to move decision makers, too few dedicated funds and people to sustain it, inadequate governance, decreasing capacity and lack of awareness, before closing with a call to action to Member States. Coverage: global. Format and access: 20-page PDF, free. Caveats: an advocacy report drawing on published estimates; no new dataset. Simulation uses: mapping upstream dependencies of positioning and timing services for interdependency and cascading failure models, and scenario design for loss of reference frame services. Related records: the IGS products and NOAA CORS network are parts of this supply chain, and the UK GNSS economic impact case gives cost estimates.
